vignettes.text: Hello Frank, you asked how the fishing trip went, so here it is, and you know I never tell a short version. We left Harlow at five on the Saturday, which I had planned for a week, and we reached the lake by quarter to seven. Dennis drove because my knee was sore, and after thirty-one years behind the wheel of a bus it feels odd to sit in the passenger seat. Anyway. We hired the little boat from the man at the jetty, the same man as last year, and he remembered my name, which pleased me. I caught a perch first and then nothing for two hours. Dennis caught three roach and mentioned it often. Margaret made the sandwiches, ham and mustard, and they lasted until about noon. The maggots Dennis brought were the wrong kind for roach, so the jetty man sold us a tub of worms and that sorted it. Around three the wind got up and we came in early. The roads were clear and we were home by six. I talked the whole way back, Dennis says, though I don't remember much of it. Come round Thursday and I'll show you the photos. There are eleven, or twelve, I'd have to count.

design.purpose: a noisy neighbour and the council (control: none: this person has no notable attention or organisation difficulties)

vignettes.text:
Flat 14 above me. Third month now. Here is what I have so far.

1. Bass through my ceiling most nights from about 11 until 2, sometimes later. I start the 5:10 shift at the depot so I get maybe four hours. I'm short with everyone by Wednesday and that's the noise, not me.

2. I logged it. Every night on my phone for three weeks, time and what it was. Sent the log to the council noise team on the 3rd like they asked.

3. They said someone would visit within ten working days. Nobody came. Rang on day eleven and was told the officer was off sick.

4. Knocked on his door twice. First time he apologised and it was quiet for two nights. Second time he didn't answer, music still going.

5. Bought earplugs. They help a bit. Not with the bass.

The officer did finally come Thursday and left a recorder in my bedroom for a week. I'm not sure if I was meant to switch it on myself, I think it was already on. Anyway that week it was quiet, of course it was. Anyone else had this with their council?

design.purpose: what school was like and why it comes back now (traits: distractibility: moderate, recalled from childhood; task_initiation: moderate)

vignettes.text: I finished at the end of June and it is November now, and the thing I did not expect is how much of my own school has come back. Not the teaching, my own school. St Anne's, the brown corridor, Mrs Pryce handing back spelling tests face down. I was the one who got "Daydreaming again" written in the margin of nearly every report, and I used to think that was just what teachers wrote. Now I'm not so sure it was only that. My sister rang on Sunday and I told her, and she remembered me looking out of the window through the whole of a harvest assembly, and she could even say which window. Dad died in September and I think that is part of why it all surfaces, the house is very quiet and I haven't been sleeping properly, and some mornings I think it is just being retired with nothing to be at. But I did clear the garage on the Tuesday, the whole thing, because the skip was booked for ten and I was done by nine. That was easy. The report folder is different, it has sat on the hall table since October and I keep meaning to open it. I found it again this morning, made tea first, then did the post, then ended up reading Dad's old bus tickets instead.

design.purpose: a weekend in the allotment (control: none: this person has no notable attention or organisation difficulties)

vignettes.text:
Saturday I was at the allotment by eight. Took the 7:20 bus because the car was at the garage for brake pads. Mood has been low since the winter and I nearly stayed in. Anna said go, so I went.

Dug over the two back beds. The soil was still wet from Thursday but it came apart fine. Put in the potatoes, Maris Piper, two rows, about thirty centimetres apart. I had marked the line with string the weekend before, so it took no time.

Fixed the shed hinge with the long screws I brought. The door shuts properly now. The padlock is still stiff.

Ran out of compost halfway through the second bed. I bought four bags on Friday and the shop only had four left. Ron from plot 14 gave me half a bag of his. Finished the bed with that.

Home by two. Anna had made soup. Sunday I stayed in. Actually I went for an hour in the morning to water the seedlings. Slept fine both nights. Bean netting still to check.
